name: NY-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Longtime incumbent Meeks with large financial advantage
Challenger Marsh has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Meeks is a well-funded incumbent in a D+24 district, while Marsh shows no measurable campaign resources; markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold.
model.watch: Any sign of a well-funded challenger surge or unusual incumbent scandal would be the main route to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-05 covers parts of Queens and the Bronx and leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 24 points. Gregory Meeks, the incumbent since 2007, is running for another term and has built a substantial financial edge, with roughly $2 million on hand and no outside spending against him. Republican challenger George Marsh has no reported fundraising or cash on hand, and no outside groups are active in the race.

No public polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's resources, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 97 percent. The seat is rated Safe D, with Meeks heavily favored to return to Congress.
